title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost for common production workloads by wiring up autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV-caching, adding quantization profile selection, and surfacing unit-economics tooling in the Optimize console. This PR implements coordinated changes across the serving runtime, the autotune service, model profiles, and the Optimize UI/backend. Key goals: 1) apply conservative batching/caching default heuristics for newly onboarded models, 2) provide model-specific quantization profile presets (8-bit, 4-bit candidates) with quick safety checks, 3) expose per-route unit-economic estimates and an autotune 'apply recommended settings' workflow.
commits_summary: Init: add autotune defaults handler and runtime flags (Aisha Khan)
Serve: add quantization_profile plumbing + selector and compatibility checks (Marco Duarte)
Optimize: unit-econ endpoints and UI integration for recommended settings (Lina Park)
Tests: integration tests for batching/caching heuristics + e2e for apply-recommendation flow (Ben Wilson)
changed_files: redwood/serving/autotune/handler.py - new autotune handler, heuristics for batch_size/prefetch/window_size
redwood/serving/runtime/kv_cache.py - cache policy flags and TTL tuning hooks
redwood/serving/runtime/batcher.cpp - add conservative default batcher thresholds and logging
redwood/optimize/backend/unit_econ_service.py - endpoints to compute per-route cost estimates and savings projection
redwood/model-registry/quant_profiles.yaml - add curated quant profiles for x86+cuda and aarch64
redwood/ci/integration/test_autotune.py - e2e tests mocking request distributions
redwood/docs/ops/autotune.md - docs for the autotune defaults and rollback guidance
redwood/infra/feature_flags.yaml - feature flag to gate rollout in prod
review_comments: Ben Wilson: Overall looks good. A couple of nits on config naming and an edge-case where small requests might get batched too aggressively - please add a safety bound.
Aisha Khan: Thanks Ben, added safety bound (min_latency_ms) and updated handler tests to cover small request distributions.
Lina Park: UX looks clean. Request: include an explicit rollback CTA in the UI after applying recommendations in case latency regressions are observed.
Aisha Khan: Added rollback CTA, and a follow-up metric to detect latency regressions for 5 minute windows. Updated unit tests and integration tests.
Marco Duarte: Quant profiles look sane. Two requests: (1) ensure 4-bit candidates are opt-in per model family, (2) add a runtime guard to skip quant when unsupported kernels detected.
Aisha Khan: Implemented opt-in per model_family flag and kernel compatibility checks with fallback to 8-bit. Added logs and metrics for skipped quantizations.
ci_checks: e2e: flaky on first run, rerun passed - 2025-02-20T20:12:00Z
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching, curated quantization profiles with opt-in 4-bit candidates, and unit-economics tooling in Optimize (recommendation + apply + rollback). Improves default cost/performance for newly onboarded models and exposes savings estimates to customers.
impact: Conservative rollout behind a feature flag. Default heuristics applied for new models only; existing pinned customer settings are unchanged. Expected median cost reduction 6-12% on inference-heavy routes in internal canaries. Added telemetry to detect regressions and automatic rollback hooks (manual rollback in UI).
migration_notes: No automatic changes to customer configs. Admins can opt-in per-model-family to enable 4-bit profiles. Operators should monitor autotune.recommendation.applied and unit_econ.savings_estimate dashboards during rollout.
testing_notes: Unit and integration tests added. Local integration harness includes synthetic request distributions (latency-sensitive, throughput-sensitive, mixed). Manual QA: ran Optimize apply/rollback flow against staging cluster with 2 model families.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive batching or quantization could regress latency or quality. Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-model-family opt-in for 4-bit, kernel compatibility checks, safety bounds on batch sizes, canary rollout behind feature flag, metrics-driven rollback and manual rollback CTA in UI.
